{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
The head chef at my culinary school would announce that health inspectors were coming tomorrow, triggering panic deep-cleans. After three years, a classmate noticed the inspections were always scheduled months in advance—our chef knew exactly when they'd arrive. He admitted he liked how 'urgency sharpens technique.'

CANDIDATE A:
The head chef at my culinary school announced that health inspectors were coming the next day—a surprise visit we hadn't expected. We did an emergency deep-clean all night. The inspection happened exactly as he said, and we passed with high marks. His warning about the real deadline helped us prepare properly.

CANDIDATE B:
My swimming coach would shout that the college scout was in the stands watching our practice. I'd push myself until I nearly drowned. The scout visits were always announced weeks ahead on the athletic calendar. Coach believed phantom pressure built champions.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:21"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both stories involve a figure in authority creating a false sense of urgency to manipulate the behavior of their students, ultimately revealing that the pressure was artificially constructed to enhance performance."}
